summary: New GET /api/alerts/trends?days=N (default 7, min 1, max 90) returns one bucket per UTC calendar day for the last N days (oldest first), each with a total count and a per-severity count (including zero-count days/severities), reusing the AlertSeverityCountsResponse shape/ordering from GET /api/alerts/summary. Invalid days (out of range or non-numeric) returns 400 ValidationProblemDetails via the existing [Range] + [ApiController] auto-validation convention.
scope_anchors: IAlertService / AlertManagementService: GetTrendsAsync + zero-fill bucket logic
IAlertRepository / AlertRepository: per-day per-severity count query over a UTC date range
New DTOs: AlertTrendsQueryRequest (Days), AlertTrendsResponse, AlertTrendBucketResponse (reuses AlertSeverityCountsResponse)
constraints: days query param: default 7, min 1, max 90; out-of-range or non-numeric must yield 400 ValidationProblemDetails via [Range] on the request DTO + [ApiController] auto-validation (no manual ModelState branch), matching AlertQueryRequest.Page/PageSize convention
Buckets are UTC calendar days, oldest first, covering exactly the last N days ending on the current UTC day
Every returned bucket must include all four severities (Low, Medium, High, Critical) with zero-count defaults where no alerts exist, in that fixed order via AlertSeverityCountsResponse
Use the injected TimeProvider for computing the current UTC day / window boundaries, not DateTime.UtcNow directly (matches CreateAsync convention)
Repository query must be a single set-based grouped query (no SELECT *, no per-day loop queries) per database-standards.md
No schema/migration change needed; query aggregates existing Alerts.CreatedDate and Alerts.Severity columns
Exceeding the compact 5-file source-file guidance is intentional here: the slice genuinely spans API, service, data-abstraction, data-SQL, and 3 new/edited DTO files plus a constants file
coverage_goals: behavior coverage: default days=7; explicit days within range; days=1 boundary; days=90 boundary; days=0 -> 400; days=91 -> 400; non-numeric days -> 400; zero-count days/severities are present and zero; bucket ordering is oldest-first; severity ordering within a bucket matches Low/Medium/High/Critical
resolved_decisions: Jira Space/Project not provided by the user; recorded as NOT_PROVIDED following the precedent set by ALERT-410 and ALERT-411 rather than blocking, since the Jira ID and full story detail were supplied directly.
